title: Causes for Recent MRT and LRT Breakdowns, and Measures to Improve Rail Reliability and Review Financial Penalties
what_it_is: Causes for Recent MRT and LRT Breakdowns, and Measures to Improve Rail Reliability and Review Financial Penalties

sections.label: Rail breakdowns and reliability questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Acting Minister for Transport about LRT and MRT breakdown investigations, safeguards, penalties, reliability factors and improvement plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport as regards the two breakdowns on the Sengkang-Punggol LRT in August 2025 (a) when will the final investigation results be released; (b) what safeguards have been put in place for adequate maintenance and safety checks for commuters and rail workers; and (c) what new technology and safety enhancements will be put in place to prevent future breakdowns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport (a) whether the Ministry can provide an update on the status of the investigation and the design review by LTA project team following the recent major disruptions of the Bukit Panjang LRT on 3 July 2025 and 19 July 2025; and (b) whether the power trips which were identified as the cause of both incidents could have been prevented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport in each year over the past five years (a) what is the number of regulatory breaches for each of the rail operators under the New Rail Financing Framework (NRFF); and (b) what are the corresponding financial penalties that have been imposed, including for the failure to provide and maintain an adequate, safe and satisfactory service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport (a) what factors resulted in MRT reliability falling to its lowest level since 2020; (b) whether any trend is observed across the spate of MRT and LRT disruptions since August 2025; (c) whether the rail infrastructure needs refreshing; and (d) what will be done to improve rail reliability and sustain achievement of the target of Mean Kilometres Between Failure to meet public expectations.

sections.label: MKBF target and recent figure
sections.summary: The target was surpassed in 2019 and remains exceeded, with about 1.7 million train-km in the 12 months to August 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We surpassed this target in 2019 and we have remained above it ever since.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: This number for the 12-month period leading up to August 2025 is approximately 1.7 million train-km.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: This is lower than our peak MKBF of over two million in 2022 and 2023, but still higher than the one million target.

sections.label: MKBF comparison with other metros
sections.summary: Singapore's recent MKBF is higher than Hong Kong MTR's but lower than Taipei Metro's.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Singapore's MKBF in recent years is higher than Hong Kong Mass Transit Railway's (MTR's), though lower than Taipei Metro's.

sections.label: Penalties for serious disruptions
sections.summary: LTA considers commuter impact in financial penalties and has imposed about four such penalties yearly over the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: LTA does consider commuter impact in the financial penalties that are imposed on operators for serious disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: And to Mr Louis Chua's question, LTA has imposed an average of around four such penalties per year in the past five years.

sections.label: Sengkang Depot substation faults
sections.summary: Two faults at a Sengkang Depot substation on 12 August cut power to parts of the NEL and SPLRT.

sentences.text: As LTA had explained, two faults occurred at a substation at Sengkang Depot on 12 August, which cut off power to several parts of the NEL and SPLRT.

sections.label: Rail Reliability Taskforce plans
sections.summary: A Rail Reliability Taskforce will renew critical components, conduct audits, and review service recovery processes.

sentences.text: But we want to take a harder look to satisfy ourselves that there is indeed no systemic problem.

This is why I announced last week that I had tasked the Chief Executive of LTA, Mr Ng Lang, to chair a Rail Reliability Taskforce which will include the Chief Executives of two MRT operators, Mr Ngien Hoon Ping of SMRT and Mr Jeffrey Sim of SBST.
First, it will bring forward the renewal of critical components, especially power supply and signalling for the NEL and the Circle Line.
Second, it will jointly conduct audits on the maintenance and operations of critical systems, including maintenance processes as well and staff training.
Third, it will review service recovery processes, so that we can better support commuters who are caught in a train disruption.
And here, the train operators have been informing commuters of service delays in excess of 10 minutes, as required by LTA.
In response to Mr Louis Chua's question, LTA has not had to impose any penalties on this in the past five years.

sections.label: Rail reliability and commuter assurance
sections.summary: The speaker acknowledges commuter frustrations and says rail reliability has improved, with the MRT system remaining among the world's most reliable despite recent disruptions.

sentences.text: I understand the frustrations and I want to assure commuters that we are doing our best to improve our performance.
We know we can do better because our rail reliability has indeed been better in the last few years.
But even with the recent disruptions, our MRT system remains one of the most reliable in the world.

sections.label: Penalties, incidents and operator requirements
sections.summary: The speaker notes the EWL breakdown penalty was reduced from $3 million to $2.4 million, cites the Rapid Transit Systems Act fine maximum, and asks about operator investment requirements for 15 incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The first, in relation to the question on the penalties and the incidents specifically, I understand that in relation to last year's East-West Line (EWL) breakdown for about six days, I think the penalty was reduced from $3 million to $2.4 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I wanted to double check, specifically on the Rapid Transit Systems Act, the operators can be fined to a maximum of higher of $1 million or 10% of the fare revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The second supplementary question, in relation to the 15 key incidents that LTA has put out last Friday, for these incidents, I note that the Government will be putting in an additional $1 billion to raise the reliability and maintenance standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What are the corresponding requirements on the part of each of the operators, in terms of the additional investments that they may have to put in?

sections.label: Penalty above one million threshold
sections.summary: The speaker states the issued penalty was well above the $1 million threshold, originally $3 million and reduced to about $2 million after appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: The penalty we have issued is well above the $1 million threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We had given them a $3 million dollar penalty and we had, after appeal, reduced their penalty to about $2 million.

sections.label: Disruption numbers year-on-year
sections.summary: The speaker says there were about 13 disruptions in the corresponding period last year, compared to 15 this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: I took a look at the number of disruptions for the corresponding period last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: It was about 13, compared to 15 this year.

sections.label: Improving standards and MKBF limits
sections.summary: The speaker says standards and quality should improve over time but zero disruptions is not possible, and MKBF is not meaningful at single-digit disruption levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: I think we have to see what we can do to try our best to improve the standards over time, improve the quality, but it is not possible for us to drive down to zero disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Therefore, looking at the MKBF, as I mentioned in my speech, it is actually not very meaningful beyond high levels of rail reliability, not meaningful when you have small numbers, single-digit disruptions.

sections.label: LTA asset ownership under framework
sections.summary: The speaker states that under the new rail financing framework, LTA is responsible for the ownership and renewal of assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Under the new rail financing framework, LTA is responsible for the ownership and renewal of assets.

sections.label: NEL connection and bus network
sections.summary: The ultimate solution is connecting the NEL to more train lines, with the Cross Island Line making it more resilient, while buses are not a good solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: The ultimate solution is to connect the NEL to more train lines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We are building the Cross Island Line, I have to try to make sure things are okay for the next five years, but I think when the Cross Island Line connects to Hougang, it will make the NEL more resilient because commuters will be able to discharge to some other routes on the train network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: In the meantime, we are looking at how to augment the bus network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: But buses, ultimately, are not a good solution because the capacity of one NEL train is 1,500 people.
